subject: Discovery recap — recommended evals, benchmarks, and stability guardrails
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Aug 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — recommended evals, benchmarks, and stability guardrails

Claire — thanks again for the intro call this afternoon. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) What we heard
- Primary goal: high-precision decisioning assistance for merchant risk scoring (low false positives).
- Expected volume: ~30M token/month during pilot, 300K calls/day peak.
- Regulatory needs: audit trail, pinning/certified snapshots for model versions, and an ops escalation path.

2) Redwood recommendations for initial evals (attachments + links)
- Candidate models: rw-instruct-13B-v2 (baseline), rw-7b-lite-quant (lower cost fallback), and rw-13b-safety-tuned (safety-sensitive checks).
- Benchmarks we will run: precision/recall on your gold set, hallucination rate on decision transcripts, and latency P95 with 512-token context.
- Artifacts attached: ledgerly_promptset_v1.csv (30 canonical prompts), ledgerly_eval_artifacts_v1.zip (sample outputs & scoring harness), snapshot-criteria.md (how we define a certified snapshot).

3) Stability & regression guardrails (high level)
- Canary rollout: default canary at 2% traffic for 24 hours; expand when KPIs stable.
- Automated regression detection: if precision drops by >3 absolute points or hallucination rate increases >2x on the golden set we trigger an alert.
- Emergency hold: ability to pin traffic to the prior certified snapshot within ~30 minutes and failover to fallback model if needed.

4) Next steps / asks of Ledgerly
- Can you confirm access for a read-only S3 bucket or sample dataset by next Tue (Aug 15)?
- Confirm legal contact for SOW & procurement so Aditya can loop them in.
- Are you OK with the 2% canary as a starting point or do you prefer a smaller initial window?

I'll follow up with a short email that spells out the rollback process in plain language for your compliance team. Attaching the artifacts now.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: ledgerly_eval_artifacts_v1.zip (zip), ledgerly_promptset_v1.csv (csv), snapshot-criteria.md (text)
From: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@ledgerly.com>

Date: Sun, 12 Aug 2028 19:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — recommended evals, benchmarks, and stability guardrails

Thanks Hannah — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifying questions before we give dev access: 

- Regression thresholds: the >3pt precision drop and 2x hallucination increase — are those hard stops or alert triggers? Who triages first?
- SLA: if we pin back to the prior snapshot, what is the expected time-to-stabilize? Any SLA credits or commitments we should document?

Also looping procurement — they asked whether the eval artifacts will contain any PII during the pilot (we will scrub, but want to confirm best practice).

—Claire
Claire Zhou
Head of Data Science, Ledgerly
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Aug 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Clarification for Ledgerly — suggested reply + escalation ladder

Hannah / Marissa — draft reply below I think we can send to Claire and procurement. I added the escalation ladder and who owns each step.

--- Forwarded message (for internal approval) ---
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@ledgerly.com>, Procurement <procurement@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Aug 2028 09:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — recommended evals, benchmarks, and stability guardrails

Claire / Procurement — quick answers and the operational plan we recommend: 

1) Regression thresholds: these are alert triggers, not instantaneous hard stops. When a threshold is exceeded the Redwood Ops on-call reviews within 15 minutes and performs a quick verification run on the golden set. If the regression is confirmed we escalate to the SE team and proceed to the rollback checklist.

2) Rollback / pin timeline: we can pin traffic to the last certified snapshot within ~30 minutes; full measured rollback (including traffic draining and validation) typically completes within 2–4 hours depending on traffic patterns and KV cache warmup. For urgent incidents we have a fast path (pin + route to fallback model) that restores parity within ~30–60 minutes.

3) SLA / credits: SLA credits and remediation are contractual — for pilots we offer an operational commitment to prioritize incidents and provide an incident report within 48 hours. We can surface credit terms in the SOW; Aditya will coordinate with procurement.

4) PII in eval artifacts: please scrub PII where possible. For pilot runs we recommend hashed identifiers and redaction of sensitive fields. If Ledgerly needs a private deployment option (VPC/on-prem) we can scope that in parallel.

Operational escalation ladder (internal owners):
- Tier 1 detection & triage: Redwood monitoring -> Ops on-call (owned by Platform SRE)
- Tier 2 verification & rollback: Solutions Engineering (Hannah) + Model Ops (Marissa)
- Tier 3 contractual remediation / credits: Sales (Aditya) + Account Exec

Related links: HubSpot deal LDG-4823 (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890) and SOW stub (DocuSign link).

If that reads OK I can send to Claire now.

Best,
Aditya
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@ledgerly.com>, Procurement <procurement@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — recommended evals, benchmarks, and stability guardrails

Claire — thanks for the questions. We recommend the following operational approach (short version for your compliance/procurement):

- Thresholds are alert triggers. Redwood ops reviews within 15 minutes; if confirmed we automatically pin traffic to the last certified snapshot. Pinning completes in ~30 minutes (fast path: pin + route to fallback model completes in 30–60 minutes).
- Full rollback validation (drain, KV warmup, QA run on golden prompts) is usually done within 2–4 hours. We will issue an incident report within 48 hours and a post-mortem if requested.
- For pilots we do not include formal SLA credits in the initial trial SOW, but we will include prioritized incident handling and a documented remediation path. If Ledgerly requires SLA credits we will add that to the commercial SOW.
- Regarding PII: please scrub or pseudonymize fields in the sample dataset. If you need a private deployment (VPC) for unredacted data we can scope that as an option.

Next steps: 
1) If procurement confirms scrubbed S3 access (or a secure transfer link) by Tue Aug 15, we will kick off model runs and share preliminary benchmark results by Fri Aug 18.
2) We’ll run the three candidate models and return a short spreadsheet with precision/recall/hallucination and latency P95.
3) If a regression is identified during rollout we will default to the pinned snapshot + fallback model and notify Ledgerly’s on-call; an incident report follows within 48 hours.

I attached the eval artifacts and the prompt set we used for the initial runs. Tell me if you want the language on the rollback timeline shortened for procurement and I’ll provide a one-paragraph statement they can copy into the SOW.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Hannah
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: ledgerly_eval_artifacts_v1.zip, ledgerly_promptset_v1.csv, snapshot-criteria.md
